prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 华东区门店2024年1—5月销量 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "门店" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 105px
  col 2: header "1月" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 39px
  col 3: header "2月" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 4: header "3月" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 5: header "4月" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 39px
  col 6: header "5月" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 39px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 392px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 391px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 392px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare monthly sales performance across six East China stores for January–May 2024, making store-level trends and month-to-month differences easy to scan.","reading":"Readers anchor on the store name in column 1, then scan horizontally across the five month columns to read a trend; they also compare vertically within a month. Equal month columns are important because those five columns share the same unit and role.","groups":["Columns 2–6 (1月–5月) form one measure group: same unit, same role, and should stay equal-width for direct comparison.","Column 1 (门店) is the row-identifier group and should remain visually distinct from the measures."],"keep_intact":["All four-digit sales values in columns 2–6 must stay on one line without breaking, wrapping, or truncation.","Month headers 1月–5月 and the header 门店 should remain intact.","Store names must remain complete; they may break only between Chinese characters, never lose characters."],"may_wrap":["Store names in column 1 can wrap to two lines; a three-line fallback is acceptable only if row height permits.","Month headers are too short to need wrapping; numeric cells should never wrap."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[91,60,60,60,60,60],"idea":"Label-first: give the store column all spare width and hold every month column at the exact minimum needed for four-digit values."},{"name":"B","widths":[76,63,63,63,63,63],"idea":"Balanced: use just enough row-label width for two-line store names and share the remaining width evenly across the five month columns."},{"name":"C","widths":[66,65,65,65,65,65],"idea":"Numeric-first: compress the row label to two-character lines so the month columns become the widest, most open numeric field."}]}
